The department emphasizes student-centered, hands-on learning grounded in Cal Poly Pomona’s “become by doing” philosophy. Students engage with real-world planning challenges through field work, design studios, and studios in GIS, climate adaptation, land-use law, and environmental assessment. With strong interdisciplinary ties to architecture, landscape architecture, and regenerative studies, the department fosters collaboration across environmental design disciplines. It holds national accreditation from the Planning Accreditation Board and receives high marks for teaching quality, professional readiness, and commitment to social equity. Students benefit from community-engaged capstone studios, internships with local agencies, and global experiences like Japan studio programs. Professional development is supported through active student chapters of the American Planning Association (APSA), the Graduate Planning Student Association, and events like the Dale Prize colloquium. Additional resources include a GIS lab, dedicated advising, laptop requirements to ensure tech readiness, outreach through alumni networks, and strong post-grad

courses.title: The City in Context - History, Politics, Environment
courses.description: [GE 4A] Focus on the American city in an historical context. Examines the rise of the American city, analyzing the evolution of its politics and built and natural environment. Develops tools to critically explore and understand contemporary cities. Field trips. Corequisite(s): URP 1040L .

courses.title: The City in Context - History, Politics, Environment-Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 4A] Focus on the American city in an historical context. Examines the rise of the American city, analyzing the evolution of its politics and built and natural environment. Develops tools to critically explore and understand contemporary cities. Field trips. Corequisite(s): URP 1040 .

courses.title: Ethnic Communities, Places, and Urban Planning
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: EWS 1051 The relationship between ethnic communities (specifically, Native Americans, African Americans, Asian Americans, and Latina and/or Latino Americans) and place in the United States. (African American includes Black Americans. Also, Latina and Latino American includes the Chicana/Chicano, Chicanx, and Latinx communities.) Interdisciplinary theories and practices of ethnic studies and place. Intersectional themes include one or more of the following: place-based policies, systemic racism, racial segregation, gentrification, immigration, community activism, environmental and economic justice, immigration, and lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer (LGBTQ) rights.

courses.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS) for Planning Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction of the concepts, principles, and the reality of using GIS. Approaches to use GIS to present data processing, visualization, and mapping. Stress the applications of geospatial data and mapping to planning related issues and phenomena using GIS technology.

courses.title: Introduction to Urban Design Theory for Planning
courses.description: Overview of conceptual and methodological frameworks in the survey and design of the built environment. Approaches to the analysis and public space. Stresses professional vocabulary, analysis visualization, representation, aesthetic, symbolic, and cultural factors. Corequisite(s): URP 2010L .

courses.title: Introduction to Urban Design Theory for Planning Laboratory
courses.description: Overview of conceptual and methodological frameworks in the survey and design of the built environment. Approaches to the analysis and public space. Stresses professional vocabulary, analysis visualization, representation, aesthetic, symbolic, and cultural factors. Corequisite(s): URP 2010 .

courses.title: Tools and Graphic Communication for Planning
courses.description: Skill development in graphic techniques as a communicative tool for planners. Includes applications for 2D and 3D design visualization techniques introduced in the context of design exercises. Corequisite(s): URP 2020L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 2010 and URP 2010L .

courses.title: Tools and Graphic Communication for Planning Laboratory
courses.description: Skill development in graphic techniques as a communicative tool for planners. Includes applications for 2D and 3D design visualization techniques introduced in the context of design exercises. Corequisite(s): URP 2020 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 2010 and URP 2010L .

courses.title: Research Approaches to Planning
courses.description: Quantitative and qualitative methods of research design; application in neighborhood, city and regional settings. Focuses on exploratory and descriptive research; introduces causality, explanatory research, inference and research ethics. Techniques of measurement, sampling, surveys and basic data analysis and communication. Corequisite(s): URP 2130L .

courses.title: Research Approaches to Planning Laboratory
courses.description: Quantitative and qualitative methods of research design; application in neighborhood, city and regional settings. Focuses on exploratory and descriptive research; introduces causality, explanatory research, inference and research ethics. Techniques of measurement, sampling, surveys and basic data analysis and communication. Corequisite(s): URP 2130 .

courses.title: Research Approaches to Planning
courses.description: Quantitative and qualitative methods of research design; application in neighborhood, city and regional settings. Focuses on exploratory and descriptive research; introduces causality, explanatory research, inference and research ethics. Techniques of measurement, sampling, surveys and basic data analysis and communication. Corequisite(s): URP 2320L , and GE Area 1B or 1B/A3.

Techniques of measurement, sampling, surveys and basic data analysis and communication. Corequisite(s): URP 2320 , and GE Area 1B or 1B/A3.

courses.title: Introduction to Urban Planning
courses.description: [GE 4C] How the planning function in government synthesizes social science information to develop plans, regulations, capital improvement strategies, and programs. Review of land use tools, General and specific plans, subdivision regulations and entitlements. Role of environmental review and public participation. Not open to URP majors Not open to URP majors
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Social Context for Urban Change
courses.description: Examines the social context that facilitates or hinders urban change. Examines forces and places that impact how individuals/groups work, live and play to understand the conditions for urban change. Includes sections on public participation and planning in socially diverse communities. Corequisite(s): URP 3050L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 1051.

courses.title: Social Context for Urban Change Laboratory
courses.description: Examines the social context that facilitates or hinders urban change. Examines forces and places that impact how individuals/groups work, live and play to understand the conditions for urban change. Includes sections on public participation and planning in socially diverse communities. Corequisite(s): URP 3050 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 1051 .

courses.title: Spatial Analysis for Urban Planning
courses.description: Using Geographic Information Systems (GIS), exploration of spatial analysis applicable to urban planning problems. Focus on intermediate GIS skills that analyze and visualize urban issues and phenomena by employing vector and raster spatial data. Corequisite(s): URP 3200L
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or C- or better in URP 1200L .

courses.title: Spatial Analysis for Urban Planning Laboratory
courses.description: Using Geographic Information Systems (GIS), exploration of spatial analysis applicable to urban planning problems. Focus on intermediate GIS skills that analyze and visualize urban issues and phenomena by employing vector and raster spatial data. Corequisite(s): URP 3200 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or C- or better in URP 1200L .

courses.title: Demography and Statistics for Planning
courses.description: Statistical analysis of quantitative information, using substantive databases from the U.S. Census and other governmental bodies; covering inferential and descriptive statistical methods. Review of collection, synthesis and organization of large databases in planning and policy analysis. Corequisite(s): URP 3320L .
courses.prerequisites: GE Area 2; and C- or better in URP 2130 and URP 2130L , or URP 3310 and URP 3310L.

courses.title: Demography and Statistics for Planning Laboratory
courses.description: Statistical analysis of quantitative information, using substantive databases from the U.S. Census and other governmental bodies; covering inferential and descriptive statistical methods. Review of collection, synthesis and organization of large databases in planning and policy analysis. Corequisite(s): URP 3320 .
courses.prerequisites: GE Area 2; and C- or better in URP 2130 and URP 2130L , or URP 3310 and URP 3310L.

courses.title: Policy Analysis for Planning
courses.description: Theories and methods for evaluating planning proposals and projects. Use of analysis techniques for urban planning policies and programs. Methodology for identifying issues and procedures and for defining, developing, obtaining approval, implementation and post adoption analysis. Corequisite(s): URP 3340L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: URP 3320 and URP 3320L .

courses.title: Policy Analysis for Planning Laboratory
courses.description: Theories and methods for evaluating planning proposals and projects. Use of analysis techniques for urban planning policies and programs. Methodology for identifying issues and procedures and for defining, developing, obtaining approval, implementation and post adoption analysis. Corequisite(s): URP 3340 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 3320 and URP 3320L .

courses.title: Plan Making History and Future
courses.description: Theoretical understanding of plan making, on design and programmatic bases incorporating current approaches. Techniques for plan making including spatial and quantitative data retrieval and analysis. Emphasis on visioning, community engagement, communicative planning, mediation/negotiation of interests and conflict resolution. Corequisite(s): URP 3350A .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 2020 , and URP 2020L or URP 2020A.

courses.title: Plan Making History and Future Activity
courses.description: Theoretical understanding of plan making, on design and programmatic bases incorporating current approaches. Techniques for plan making including spatial and quantitative data retrieval and analysis. Emphasis on visioning, community engagement, communicative planning, mediation/negotiation of interests and conflict resolution. Corequisite(s): URP 3350 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 2020 , and URP 2020L or URP 2020A.

courses.title: Urban Systems Infrastructure
courses.description: Survey of major infrastructure systems such as transportation, water, sanitation, electric power, information. Political economy of their origins, social justice implications, and potential for change. Review of responsible public and private agencies and the interaction among them. Field trips. Corequisite(s): URP 3370L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 1200L.

courses.title: Urban Systems Infrastructure Laboratory
courses.description: Survey of major infrastructure systems such as transportation, water, sanitation, electric power, information. Political economy of their origins, social justice implications, and potential for change. Review of responsible public and private agencies and the interaction among them. Field trips. Corequisite(s): URP 3370 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 1200L.

courses.title: Urban Systems - Climate Change and Environment
courses.description: Understanding ecological systems for urban and regional planning, exploring local, regional, and global impacts of human activity. Role of cities and regions in contributing to global climate change. Planning strategies for resilience, including climate change adaptation.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 1040 , URP 1040L , URP 2010 , and URP 2010L .

courses.title: Planning and Land Use Law
courses.description: Legal framework for planning, including review of legal processes, constitutional rights, general plan, zoning, subdivision management, and design review. Integration of local planning with regional sustainability planning. Basic structure of state and federal planning and environmental laws, including judicial opinions. Corequisite(s): URP 3510A .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 1040 and URP 1040L .

courses.title: Planning and Land Use Law Activity
courses.description: Legal framework for planning, including review of legal processes, constitutional rights, general plan, zoning, subdivision management, and design review. Integration of local planning with regional sustainability planning. Basic structure of state and federal planning and environmental laws, including judicial opinions. Corequisite(s): URP 3510 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 1040 and URP 1040L .

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Placemaking: Theories, Methods, and Practices
courses.description: [GE 3C] What are the physical, social, and cultural factors that contribute to the development of great urban places? This course introduces students to mainstream and critical placemaking theories, methods, and practices. The course will draw from the humanities, including philosophy, history, aesthetics/ critical theory, and literature to ground students’ theoretical understanding of ‘space, ‘place,’ and social belonging. Special attention is paid to the placemaking contributions of historically marginalized people and communities, including communities of color, immigrants, women, and LGBTQIX people.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Evolution of American Cities and the Planning Movement
courses.description: [GE 4C] History of urban development in the United States since the 19th Century in a comparative perspective. Emphasis on the role of planning and the institutional, cultural, and economic determinants of the evolution of urban patterns. Special emphasis on the Los Angeles Metropolitan region.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Urban Design in Europe
courses.description: [GE 4C] The evolution of civic design in Western Europe, from the mid-nineteenth century. Urban design paradigms, and the role of planners, civic leaders, and visionaries in shaping the aesthetics of European urban places. An introduction to European cities by consideration of their civic, residential, and commercial landscapes.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: The Just City
courses.description: [GE 4C] How do cities evolve into more or less fair places? This course highlights theories of urban justice, methods for advocacy and equity planning, and best practice case studies to explore the roles of planners in advancing social equity and justice.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Planning with Minority Communities and Advocacy
courses.description: An overview of planning issues that impact racial minorities and working-class communities, particularly in the Los Angeles area. The field of planning offers distinct, place-based perspectives and opportunities for improving historically, disenfranchised communities.

courses.title: Public Participation
courses.description: Multifaceted strategies that planners engage in with various parties having diverse and, sometimes, conflicting interests. Private interests, such as developers and corporations, along with individuals and groups engaged in social activism. Notions of communicative rationality.

courses.title: Community Planning Studio Preparation Activity
courses.description: Demographic and community research will be conducted to understand the physical, social, and political contexts of their planning studio. Related tasks include introductions to the studio client and developing scopes and schedules of work for URP 4320.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 3050 , URP 3050L , URP 3320 , URP 3320L , URP 3350 , and URP 3350A .

courses.title: Community Planning Studio
courses.description: Application of research, analysis, and community planning procedures to a real world planning problem. Practice of public participation and produce a final Strategic Plan for their client. Plans include community visions, objectives, implementation schedules, and benchmarking components. Corequisite(s): URP 4320L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 4310A .

courses.title: Community Planning Studio Laboratory
courses.description: Application of research, analysis, and community planning procedures to a real world planning problem. Practice of public participation and produce a final Strategic Plan for their client. Plans include community visions, objectives, implementation schedules, and benchmarking components. Corequisite(s): URP 4320 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 4310A .

courses.title: Affordable Housing and Community Development
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 5340 Evolving theory and processes of economic and community development. Explores social and economic theories in the regional development processes. Research into regional, national, and global influences on urban communities. Exploration of long-range self-sufficiency and sustainability processes. Corequisite(s): URP 4340A .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 1040 , URP 1040L , URP 2010 , URP 2010L , URP 2130 or URP 2320 , and URP 2130L or URP 2320L .

courses.title: Affordable Housing and Community Development Activity
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 5340A Evolving theory and processes of economic and community development. Explores social and economic theories in the regional development processes. Research into regional, national, and global influences on urban communities. Exploration of long-range self-sufficiency and sustainability processes. Corequisite(s): URP 4340 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 1040 , URP 1040L , URP 2010 , URP 2010L , URP 2130 or URP 2320 , and URP 2130L or URP 2320L .

courses.title: Sustainable Transportation Planning
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 5350 Understanding factors in land use, travel behavior, and process that shape sustainable transportation planning and policy choices. Examination of policy and built environment issues in transportation planning from the perspective of sustainability. Planning and evaluation methods in transportation policy. Corequisite(s): URP 4350L .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; or C- or better in URP 3370 and URP 3370L .

courses.title: Sustainable Transportation Planning Laboratory
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 5350L Understanding factors in land use, travel behavior, and process that shape sustainable transportation planning and policy choices. Examination of policy and built environment issues in transportation planning from the perspective of sustainability. Planning and evaluation methods in transportation policy. Corequisite(s): URP 4350 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, or C- or better in URP 3370 and URP 3370L .

courses.title: Budgeting and Finance in the Public Sector
courses.description: Introduction to public finance, focusing on local government financing methods and techniques. Operational and capital budgeting. Tax and other revenues. Short and long term financing techniques including for local and regional infrastructure. Procedures for defining capital needs and budgeting. Techniques to include exactions, assessment districts, tax districts, bonds, special sales and other taxes, local, state and federal financing. Methods of public/private partnerships for infrastructure financing.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; or C- or better in URP 3370 and URP 3370L .

courses.title: Planning for Infrastructure
courses.description: Examination of a broad range of non-transportation infrastructure in comparative urban contexts. Considers public and private sector interests, and social justice aspects. Investigation of the influence of the planning field in infrastructure trends and policies, especially relating to resilience.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, or C- or better in URP 3370 and URP 3370L .

courses.title: Field Internship
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 5410 Practical application of urban and regional planning through supervised, unpaid fieldwork. Written report and evaluation of experience required. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 3 units.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor Consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Maximum of 3 units.

courses.title: Ethics Writing for Planning Activity
courses.description: Improving professional writing and understanding ethics in planning. Students discuss ethical issues and write short reflection papers on the issues which include the AICP Code of Ethics, the ethical role of the planner, environmental ethics, corruption, ethical design, and planning theory and ethics.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 3340 , URP 3340L , URP 3350 , URP 3350A , URP 3370 , URP 3370L , and URP 3380 .

courses.title: Land Use Entitlements and Urban Design Policy
courses.description: Review of the development of land use entitlements and urban design policies. Emphasis on the legal basis for entitlements and the application of general plan and development code requirements in the land use entitlement process, as well as the integration of these processes with urban design policies and designs. Topics covered include general plans, zoning, specific plans, site plan review, subdivisions, landscape plans, and design guidelines/architectural review. Corequisite(s): URP 4510A .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; or C- or better in URP 2020 , URP 2020L or URP 2020A, URP 3510 , and URP 3510A .

courses.title: Land Use Entitlements and Urban Design Policy Activity
courses.description: Review of the development of land use entitlements and urban design policies. Emphasis on the legal basis for entitlements and the application of general plan and development code requirements in the land use entitlement process, as well as the integration of these processes with urban design policies and designs. Topics covered include general plans, zoning, specific plans, site plan review, subdivisions, landscape plans, and design guidelines/architectural review. Corequisite(s): URP 4510 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; or C- or better in URP 2020 , URP 2020L or URP 2020A, URP 3510 , and URP 3510A .

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Supervised original research on a topic relevant to urban and regional planning. Implementation of a research design. Production of completed research paper or project design. Production and presentation of poster. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing, and C- or better in URP 4600AW .

courses.title: Professional Practice for Planning
courses.description: Integration and application of political analysis, planning theory, the professional code of ethics, and professional skills to practical planning situations. Advanced review of key concepts, including justice, community, and beauty in design. Presentations by and discussions with a variety of private and public planning professionals.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 3340 , URP 3340L , and URP 3380 .

courses.title: Environmental Assessment
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 5660 Methods and approaches to assessing environmental impacts and mitigations of such impacts for proposed public and private projects with emphasis on the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and Federal environmental laws.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, or C- or better in URP 3510 and URP 3510A .

courses.title: Planning in a Global Economy
courses.description: [GE 4C] Major issues confronting residents, planners and other professionals working in developing nations. Theory and practice of development planning. Factors associated with major problems and mainstream and alternative approaches to addressing urban change in a development context.
courses.prerequisites: Junior, senior, or graduate standing. Completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: International Planning
courses.description: Comparative study of planning practices and policies at global level. Examines how local communities, international agreements and economic and political powers influence development. Reviews topical trends, case study projects, themes of governmental and NGO-based assistance.

courses.title: California Water
courses.description: [GE 4C] Review of the history of the water system and water policy in California, including the major social, political, and environmental issues. Introduction to water law for non-lawyers and applies concepts of sustainability to water policy.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Neighborhood Development Processes
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 5830 Introduction to the roles of the private and public sectors in the design and development of urban projects. Focus is on the procedural aspects of development, methods of finance, project feasibility analysis, project evaluation and review, and government incentives. Corequisite(s): URP 4830A .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; or C- or better in URP 3510 and URP 3510A .

courses.title: Neighborhood Development Processes Activity
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 5830A Introduction to the roles of the private and public sectors in the design and development of urban projects. Focus is on the procedural aspects of development, methods of finance, project feasibility analysis, project evaluation and review, and government incentives. Corequisite(s): URP 4830 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; or C- or better in URP 3510 and URP 3510A .

courses.title: Urban Design Principles and Applications
courses.description: Physical and urban design theories, principles, and applications. Best practices in district, neighborhood design, and site design. Computer applications for development and communication of physical design schemes. Corequisite(s): URP 4850L .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; or C- or better in URP 2020 , and URP 2020L or URP 2020A.

courses.title: Urban Design Principles and Applications Laboratory
courses.description: Physical and urban design theories, principles, and applications. Best practices in district, neighborhood design, and site design. Computer applications for development and communication of physical design schemes. Corequisite(s): URP 4850 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; or C- or better in URP 2020 , and URP 2020L or URP 2020A.

courses.title: Environmental Policy
courses.description: Review of major concepts in environmental planning, including sustainability, resiliency, risk management, and environmental ethics. Overview of major local, regional, state, national, and global environmental policies. Methods of ecological management.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, or C- or better in URP 3510 and URP 3510A .

courses.title: Transportation Methods and Analysis
courses.description: Introduces transportation modeling and travel demand forecasting methods and software. Emphasis is placed on both the conventional four-step and activity based modeling approaches and the fundamentals of travel behavior from a theoretical, applied and practical perspective. The course employs transportation modeling software. Corequisite(s): URP 4890L .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, or C- or better in URP 3320 and URP 3320L .

courses.title: Transportation Methods and Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: Introduces transportation modeling and travel demand forecasting methods and software. Emphasis is placed on both the conventional four-step and activity based modeling approaches and the fundamentals of travel behavior from a theoretical, applied and practical perspective. The course employs transportation modeling software. Corequisite(s): URP 4890 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, or C- or better in URP 3320 and URP 3320L .

courses.title: Advanced GIS
courses.description: Advanced application of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) including vector and raster based spatial analysis. Emphasis is placed object oriented-data modeling, network analysis, spatial statistics, automation of GIS analysis, and 3-dimensional visualization techniques. Corequisite(s): URP 4900L .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or C- or better in URP 1200L .

courses.title: Advanced GIS Laboratory
courses.description: Advanced application of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) including vector and raster based spatial analysis. Emphasis is placed object oriented-data modeling, network analysis, spatial statistics, automation of GIS analysis, and 3-dimensional visualization techniques. Corequisite(s): URP 4900 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or C- or better in URP 1200L .

courses.title: Planning for Climate Change
courses.description: Scientific, economic, cultural, and ecological aspects of global climate change. Addresses greenhouse-gas mitigation methods and adaptation strategies for cities and regions. Emphasizes the development of climate action plans using resiliency planning methods. Corequisite(s): URP 4910A .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or C- or better in URP 3380 .

courses.title: Planning for Climate Change Activity
courses.description: Scientific, economic, cultural, and ecological aspects of global climate change. Addresses greenhouse-gas mitigation methods and adaptation strategies for cities and regions. Emphasizes the development of climate action plans using resiliency planning methods. Corequisite(s): URP 4910 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or C- or better in URP 3380 .

courses.title: How Planning Works
courses.description: Overview of local government planning practices including general plans, zoning codes, CEQA, the entitlement process and coordination with other public agencies and special districts. Knowledge and skillsets that planners must have such as the principles of microeconomics and algebra.

courses.title: Planning and Place
courses.description: Reviews the development of social and economic structure of cities and regions. Explores the historical development and current issues involving human habitats in developed and developing countries in the context of forces that shape and affect possibilities for cities and regions.

courses.title: Land Use Planning Law and Intergovernmental Relations
courses.description: Introduces the intergovernmental legal framework for planning. Legal processes and constitutional property rights. Local general plans, zoning, subdivision management, and design controls and their integration with regional planning. Major state and federal environmental and planning related programs, policies and requirements.

courses.title: Planning for Environmental Sustainability
courses.description: Introduction to the theories and practices of planning for environmental sustainability with an emphasis on equity, resilience, and real-world application. Through hyflex lectures and hands-on computer labs, learn the “Three Es” of sustainability and apply spatial tools (ArcGIS Pro) and basic statistics (SPSS/Excel) to analyze urban issues such as climate change, land use and growth management, transportation, water and public health, disaster resilience, green infrastructure, and environmental justice. Team-based assignments, quizzes, and lab exercises connect concepts to practice communicating findings to professional and public audiences.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and C- or better in URP 5060 .

courses.title: Planning Ideas and Actions
courses.description: Understanding core planning ideas through the lens of procedural planning theory. Alternative conceptions of rationality and the public interest. Linking knowledge and action. Tracing the co-evolution of society and planning, including public participation.

courses.title: Research Approaches to Planning
courses.description: Introduction to qualitative and quantitative research methods. Techniques of measurement and sampling for gathering original data. Assessing and using secondary data sources. Descriptive statistics and introduction to inferential methods. Application of data analysis toward the study of public policy issues. Corequisite(s): URP 5210L .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and C- or better in URP 5120 .

courses.title: Research Approaches to Planning Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to qualitative and quantitative research methods. Techniques of measurement and sampling for gathering original data. Assessing and using secondary data sources. Descriptive statistics and introduction to inferential methods. Application of data analysis toward the study of public policy issues. Corequisite(s): URP 5210 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and C- or better in URP 5120 .

courses.title: Policy Analysis and Advanced Research Methods
courses.description: Evaluation methods for assessing the impact of public policies and private decisions on the public welfare, using quantitative and qualitative analytic tools. Emphasis is on skillful application of anticipatory and retrospective policy analysis to planning problems, and critical reflection on the strengths and weaknesses of economic-based evaluation. Corequisite(s): URP 5230A .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, and C- or better in URP 5210 and URP 5210L .

courses.title: Policy Analysis and Advanced Research Methods Activity
courses.description: Evaluation methods for assessing the impact of public policies and private decisions on the public welfare, using quantitative and qualitative analytic tools. Emphasis is on skillful application of anticipatory and retrospective policy analysis to planning problems, and critical reflection on the strengths and weaknesses of economic-based evaluation. Corequisite(s): URP 5230 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 5210 and URP 5210L ; or URP 521 and URP 521L.

courses.title: GIS for Planning
courses.description: Introduction to geographic information systems. GIS data visualization and processing for the field of urban and regional planning. Introductory spatial data management and intermediate uses of GIS for spatial analysis will be introduced. Corequisite(s): URP 5250L .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing.

courses.title: GIS for Planning Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to geographic information systems. GIS data visualization and processing for the field of urban and regional planning. Introductory spatial data management and intermediate uses of GIS for spatial analysis will be introduced. Corequisite(s): URP 5250 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing.

courses.title: Affordable Housing and Community Development
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 4340 Evolving theory and processes of economic and community development. Explores social and economic theories in the regional development processes. Research into regional, national, and global influences on urban communities. Exploration of long-range self-sufficiency and sustainability processes. Corequisite(s): URP 5340A .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing.

courses.title: Affordable Housing and Community Development Activity
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 4340A Evolving theory and processes of economic and community development. Explores social and economic theories in the regional development processes. Research into regional, national, and global influences on urban communities. Exploration of long-range self-sufficiency and sustainability processes. Corequisite(s): URP 5340 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing.

courses.title: Sustainable Transportation Planning
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 4350 Understanding factors in land use, travel behavior, and process that shape sustainable transportation planning and policy choices. Examination of policy and built environment issues in transportation planning from the perspective of sustainability. Planning and evaluation methods in transportation policy. Corequisite(s): URP 5350L .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; or C- or better in URP 3370 and URP 3370L .

courses.title: Sustainable Transportation Planning Laboratory
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 4350L Understanding factors in land use, travel behavior, and process that shape sustainable transportation planning and policy choices. Examination of policy and built environment issues in transportation planning from the perspective of sustainability. Planning and evaluation methods in transportation policy. Corequisite(s): URP 5350 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, or C- or better in URP 3370 and URP 3370L .

courses.title: Environmental Policy
courses.description: Theories, ethics and methods of environmental planning in an intergovernmental context. Analysis of environmental equity in facility siting and urban design. Review of environmental elements for general plans, risk analysis, and habitat conservation planning.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Urban Design
courses.description: Economic, demographic, and cultural determinants of urban growth. Principles of land-use organization and design at area-wide, neighborhood, and site levels. Policy approaches to translating design goals and intent to guidelines and policy. Corequisite(s): URP 5380L .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Urban Design Laboratory
courses.description: Economic, demographic, and cultural determinants of urban growth. Principles of land-use organization and design at area-wide, neighborhood, and site levels. Policy approaches to translating design goals and intent to guidelines and policy. Corequisite(s): URP 5380 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Planning for Community Change
courses.description: Exploration of theoretics and praxis of planning for social change. Topics include successful community change models, direct organizing, asset based community development, capacity building, youth participation, and just sustainability. Lab covers tools for community action. May involve community-based projects. Corequisite(s): URP 5400L .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; and C- or better in URP 5050 , URP 5210 , and URP 5210L .

courses.title: Planning for Community Change Laboratory
courses.description: Exploration of theoretics and praxis of planning for social change. Topics include successful community change models, direct organizing, asset based community development, capacity building, youth participation, and just sustainability. Lab covers tools for community action. May involve community-based projects. Corequisite(s): URP 5400 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; and C- or better in URP 5050 , URP 5210 , and URP 5210L .

courses.title: Field Internship
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 4410 Practical application of urban and regional planning through supervised, unpaid fieldwork. Written report and evaluation of experience required. Work expectation is 150 hours of fieldwork per unit granted. Maximum 2 units.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor Consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Maximum 2 units.

courses.title: Methods in Leadership and Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Examines foundational theories and practices in leadership and entrepreneurship in planning and emerging fields. Not limited to planning, explores best practices and successful case studies to foster leadership skills and entrepreneurial ventures among graduates for the public good. Corequisite(s): URP 5430A .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Methods in Leadership and Entrepreneurship Activity
courses.description: Examines foundational theories and practices in leadership and entrepreneurship in planning and emerging fields. Not limited to planning, course explores best practices and successful case studies to foster leadership skills and entrepreneurial ventures among graduates for the public good. Corequisite(s): URP 5430 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Environmental Assessment
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 4660 Methods and approaches to assessing environmental impacts and mitigations of such impacts for proposed public and private projects with emphasis on the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and Federal environmental laws.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, or C- or better in URP 3510 and URP 3510A .

courses.title: Neighborhood Development Processes
courses.description: Dual Listed as: URP 4830 Introduction to the roles of the private and public sectors in the design and development of urban projects. Focus is on the procedural aspects of development, methods of finance, project feasibility analysis, project evaluation and review, and government incentives. Corequisite(s): URP 5830A .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; or C- or better in URP 2020 , URP 2020L , URP 3510 , and URP 3510A .

courses.title: Graduate Studio Preparation
courses.description: Planning and community design studio project framing and goal formulation. Quantitative and qualitative analysis of project. Physical, social, cultural, and political context of client. Theory, process, design and method for strategic planning. Preparation of strategy and schedule for Graduate Studio.
courses.prerequisites: Advancement to candidacy.

courses.title: Graduate Planning Studio
courses.description: Plan, policy, or implementation proposal addressing a real world planning problem. Synthesis of planning and community design issues and data identified and analyzed in Graduate Studio Preparation. Research, quantitative and qualitative analysis, community engagement and presentation skills emphasized. Corequisite(s): URP 6420L .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and C- or better in URP 6400 .

courses.title: Graduate Planning Studio Laboratory
courses.description: Plan, policy, or implementation proposal addressing a real world planning problem. Synthesis of planning and community design issues and data identified and analyzed in Graduate Studio Preparation. Research, quantitative and qualitative analysis, community engagement and presentation skills emphasized. Corequisite(s): URP 6420 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and C- or better in URP 6400 .

courses.title: Leadership and Ethics Seminar
courses.description: Identification of personal work style, group dynamics, management approaches, and leadership skills for planning in the public, non-profit, and private sectors. Case-based development of ethical reasoning. Identification of personal and professional ethical standards.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and C- or better in URP 5120 .

courses.title: Professional Practice for Urban and Regional Planning
courses.description: Review of alternative planning career paths in planning disciplines, settings (local, regional, state, federal, and international), and private and non-profit sectors. Planning ethics. Organizational culture and planning management. Planning communication
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 5010 , or URP 501 and URP 501L; and C- or better in URP 5120 , or URP 512 and URP 512A.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research in a specialized area, under the direction of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Independent Research
courses.description: Individual study/investigation and research in a specialized area proposed by the student with the approval, and under the supervision, of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Capstone Project Preparation Activity - Client Project
courses.description: Identify potential clients and develop their own client project topics. Students gain understanding of the client and client’s needs for the project, develop goals and objectives for the project, prepare a scope of work, schedule and analysis methodology.
courses.prerequisites: Advancement to candidacy.

courses.title: Capstone Project Preparation Activity - Thesis
courses.description: Understanding of the Master’s thesis research procedures, administrative requirements, human subjects regulations, and deadlines. Selection of research theme, literature review, formulation of research question, and methodology design for the Master’s thesis.
courses.prerequisites: Advancement to candidacy.

courses.title: Client Project
courses.description: Under faculty supervision, students undertake the project developed in Client Project Preparation using planning concepts and techniques to solve planning problems and identify improvement opportunities for the selected client. The students write recommendations and implementation reports and make a formal presentation to client.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 6941A and Advancement to candidacy.

courses.title: Master’s Thesis
courses.description: Development of a terminal Master’s thesis, under the supervision of a Thesis Committee. Selection of Thesis Committee members, conducts original research, and writes the thesis within a planning-related theoretical framework.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in URP 6942A and Advancement to candidacy.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Continuation
courses.description: Enrollment in this course allows candidates that have enrolled in the maximum number of thesis or project units to maintain resident status in order to receive university services.
